name: Grande Mosquée de Bamako
subtitle: Monumental central mosque in Bozola redeveloped in Saudi-Sudanese modernist architecture in the 1970s.

facts.label: Original site
facts.value: Pre-colonial mudbrick mosque built by Bozo community

facts.label: Current edifice
facts.value: Rebuilt in the late 1970s with Saudi funding, featuring soaring minarets and expansive prayer halls

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Bozola quarter, north of the Niger River in central Bamako

parts.text: The primary Islamic place of worship in the Malian capital, situated north of the Niger River in the central Bozola district. Built on the site of an earlier pre-colonial mudbrick mosque and reconstructed in the late 1970s with assistance from the Saudi government, this imposing white-and-sandstone mosque features soaring minarets visible across central Bamako, serving as the spiritual anchor for national Islamic holidays and Friday communal prayers.

gaps: Diocese and Islamic council historical records on the pre-colonial structure are partially digitized.
